findings.problem: The gate trusts unsigned, user-authored JSON as independent-review evidence.
findings.evidence: engineering-review.schema.json contains no signature or trusted provenance field, and loadReview() only parses and schema-validates JSON. engineering-os.test.cjs:81-92 manufactures reviewer="codex" with disposition="APPROVE" locally, and lines 208-212 assert that this fabricated record clears the FULL gate. The packet permits builder-control/review-sign.cjs, but `test -e builder-control/review-sign.cjs` returned 1.
findings.impact: The builder can create its own Codex or Grok approval record and satisfy the supposedly independent review gate without either reviewer running. This defeats the central separation-of-duties control.
findings.requiredCorrection: Require trusted review provenance. Bind an authenticated attestation to the subject hash, immutable packet-content hash, reviewer identity/model, disposition, and findings. Verify that attestation inside gateDone rather than trusting the reviewer string.
findings.verificationMethod: Prove that a hand-authored but otherwise valid APPROVE record is rejected, that a trusted adapter-produced record is accepted, and that changing any attested field invalidates the record.

findings.location: Engineering OS subject/classification steps, lines 146-154 and 207-210
findings.problem: The unavailable-base fallback computes an empty subject on a clean checkout and then explicitly downgrades it to LIGHT, skipping the binding gate.
findings.evidence: The fallback calls `engineering-os.cjs --subject --json` with no base. computeSubject() at engineering-os.cjs:180-186 consequently runs `git diff --name-only HEAD`, which is empty in a clean Actions checkout. Workflow lines 207-210 then set lane=LIGHT for zero subject paths, and line 238 skips the review gate for LIGHT.
findings.impact: First-push, force-push, workflow-dispatch, or other unavailable-base runs can report green without classifying or reviewing any files in the commit.
findings.requiredCorrection: Use `git diff-tree --root --no-commit-id -r HEAD` or another exact HEAD-file range for the fallback, and fail closed if no trustworthy range can be established. Never special-case an unknown empty subject as LIGHT.
findings.verificationMethod: Run the workflow with an all-zero or unavailable base and assert that HEAD's changed files are present, control files classify FULL/high-risk, and the required-review gate executes.

findings.location: EVIDENCE_EXCLUDE and gateDone packet handling, lines 162-167 and 709-725
findings.problem: Reviews are not bound to immutable task intent or packet authorization, and the gate never checks subject paths against filesAllowed.
findings.evidence: All builder-control/packets/** files are excluded from the subject hash. Review records bind only packetId, and gateDone merely runs packet schema validation plus specCheck. `rg -n "filesAllowed|allowsProtectedPaths|preflight" builder-control/engineering-os.cjs` returned no authorization check, apart from an unrelated comment.
findings.impact: A packet can be changed after review while retaining its packetId without invalidating the review. A valid but unrelated packet can also be used for subject paths it never authorized.
findings.requiredCorrection: Bind reviews to a packet-content or authorization digest and invoke the canonical Builder Control authorization check over every subject path, including protected-path authorization.
findings.verificationMethod: After approval, change the packet objective, source pins, filesAllowed, or authorization while keeping packetId constant and assert the gate reports stale binding. Also assert an out-of-scope subject path is refused.

findings.problem: Any bound record can supersede a record from a different reviewer.
findings.evidence: The code collects every supersedes value into one global Set and removes matching reviewIds before grouping by reviewer. It never verifies that the replacement and replaced records have the same reviewer, despite the schema describing supersession as resolution of duplicate records from one reviewer.
findings.impact: A Codex, human, or builder-controlled record can remove a Copilot or Grok rejection and its blocking findings from the active evidence set.
findings.requiredCorrection: Permit supersession only when both records are bound to the same subject and packet, have the same reviewer identity, and the replacement explicitly re-evaluates the earlier verdict. Reject nonexistent, cross-reviewer, cyclic, or self-superseding references.
findings.verificationMethod: Add negative tests proving Codex cannot supersede Copilot or Grok, a record cannot supersede itself, and a same-reviewer replacement remains valid only under the complete binding rules.

findings.problem: Actual reviewer execution bypasses the model router's availability, cost, and data-sensitivity controls.
findings.evidence: canonGate() rejects only enabled=false or availability=DISABLED, so UNVERIFIED or BLOCKED tools remain runnable. runTool() directly spawns Grok and never calls routeRole() or meteredAuthorization(). MODEL-ROUTING-POLICY.json:83-108 classifies Grok as METERED and requires a named human plus cap. Additionally, `routeRole('implementation-review',{dataClass:'CONFIDENTIAL'})` returned ok:true even though Codex maxDataClass is INTERNAL because the model policy and tool canon use incompatible data-class vocabularies.
findings.impact: The system can execute an unverified or metered reviewer without authorization and can allow data above a model's declared ceiling.
findings.requiredCorrection: Use one executable routing path for every launch. It must require AVAILABLE evidence, validate a single canonical data-class vocabulary, enforce capability and cost authorization, and pass the resulting route token/bounds to the adapter.
findings.verificationMethod: Assert that UNVERIFIED/BLOCKED Grok, missing budget approval, unknown data classes, and data above INTERNAL all prevent spawn; then prove a fully authorized eligible route launches once.

findings.problem: Reviewers do not receive the pinned specifications or deterministic-test evidence required by the approved packet, and the executable start flow schedules reviews before those checks.
findings.evidence: The prompts contain only packet.objective, subject paths, and diff. There is no sourceOfTruth content/hash or test output. The packet constraint at lines 13-14 requires authoritative paths, test evidence, and explicit unverified items. engineering-os.cjs:984-991 prints reviewer commands first and only runs deterministic checks later inside --gate-done, contradicting AI-ENGINEERING-OS.md:97-109.
findings.impact: A reviewer can approve without seeing the actual acceptance contract or whether tests passed, while expensive reviews run before cheaper falsifiers.
findings.requiredCorrection: Run and persist deterministic evidence before review. Supply bounded pinned-spec content/hashes, command results, and explicit unverified items to each reviewer, and refuse review execution when required inputs are absent.
findings.verificationMethod: Inspect a dry-run prompt and prove it contains the pinned requirements and actual test evidence; assert --start orders deterministic validation before any model invocation.

findings.problem: The canonical evidence ledger is neither concurrency-safe nor idempotent despite the new schema claiming both behavior and operation identifiers.
findings.evidence: writeLedger() constructs `[...oldEntries, newEntry]`. If another process appended meanwhile, it accepts a longer on-disk ledger after comparing only the old prefix, then overwrites it with its stale array, losing the concurrent entry. appendEntry() always appends and never checks operationId. ledger-entry.schema.json:172-175 nevertheless claims a repeated operationId is a no-op.
findings.impact: Concurrent agents can silently erase audit evidence, and retries can create duplicate operations or events. This corrupts the sole event/evidence authority.
findings.requiredCorrection: Implement atomic serialized writes using a lock or the approved SQLite WAL durable store, require exact current-version checks, and enforce operationId uniqueness transactionally before executing or recording external effects.
findings.verificationMethod: Run parallel append stress tests and prove every unique entry survives exactly once; append the same operationId concurrently and prove one durable record and one no-op result.

findings.problem: The dashboard projector cannot project the exact committed base-to-head subject used by CI.
findings.evidence: projectEngineering() passes only --packet and --subject-sha to gateDone. parseArgs() accepts no --base, --head, --changed, or --diff-lines. gateDone therefore recomputes from `git diff HEAD`, which is empty after the reviewed changes are committed, and docs lane classification also lacks its required line count.
findings.impact: A clean committed worktree can display an empty or mismatched subject, wrong lane, and wrong blockers instead of the PR or checkpoint being inspected.
findings.requiredCorrection: Project a persisted canonical run/subject record or accept and forward the exact base, head, paths, and line count used by the gate. Do not reconstruct workflow truth from the current working-tree diff.
findings.verificationMethod: In a clean checkout containing a committed reviewed change, generate state for its base/head and assert the dashboard subject hash, paths, lane, and reviewer requirements exactly match CI.

findings.location: header and event rendering, lines 259-265 and 388-400
findings.problem: The dashboard collapses materially different process states into false PASS or BLOCKED labels.
findings.evidence: Any truthy engineering verdict other than BLOCKED is rendered as PASS, so READY_FOR_DETERMINISTIC_VALIDATION appears PASS even though checks have not run. Every non-PASS ledger event is rendered BLOCKED, including FAILED integration operations, although ledger-entry.schema.json explicitly distinguishes FAILED from governance BLOCKED.
findings.impact: The command center misreports the exact process truth it exists to expose and can cause operators to treat unvalidated work as passed or connector failures as policy refusals.
findings.requiredCorrection: Render the exact canonical verdict and event status with complete glyph/style mappings. Never translate readiness into PASS or FAILED into BLOCKED.
findings.verificationMethod: Add behavioral rendering tests proving READY_FOR_DETERMINISTIC_VALIDATION remains distinct from PASS and PASS, BLOCKED, FAILED, INCOMPLETE, and IMPORTED remain distinguishable end to end.

findings.location: PREREQS/OS_FILES and post-install instructions, lines 40-89 and 205-213
findings.problem: The installer reports a complete package but omits files required by its own recommended verification.
findings.evidence: OS_FILES includes builder-control/test/engineering-os.test.cjs, whose REAL_PACKET hardcodes builder-control/packets/ENGINEERING-OS-V1.json, but the packet is absent from both installer manifests. A module probe also returned false for the packet, hosting README, workflow, and .gitignore. The installer test only verifies files named by those same incomplete manifests rather than executing the installed suite.
findings.impact: A successful empty-repository install cannot run the instructed engineering-os test and lacks automatic CI activation and generated-state ignore behavior.
findings.requiredCorrection: Make installed tests self-contained or include their fixtures, install or deterministically patch the complete CI/ignore package, and validate dependency compatibility rather than mere file presence.
findings.verificationMethod: Install into an empty temporary Git repository and run every command printed under NEXT, the complete CI fixture block, state generation, and authenticated dashboard startup successfully.

findings.problem: The approved V1 vertical slice remains materially incomplete.
findings.evidence: The contract requires a durable state machine, SQLite WAL store, leases, heartbeats, stale-run recovery, objective intake, isolated-worktree execution, watchdog sequencing, cost tracking, checkpoint/rollback controls, and end-to-end negative proofs. Repository search found no executable SQLite, WAL, lease, heartbeat, or RECOVERY_REQUIRED implementation in the changed runtime. aegis-state.cjs:288-291 permanently reports runtime and checkpoint UNVERIFIED.
findings.impact: The change delivers a gate CLI, static routing data, projector, and read-only dashboard slice, but not the executable local-first command center or complete operating loop stated in the objective.
findings.requiredCorrection: Implement the smallest complete durable vertical slice without weakening the approved contract: objective intake through routed build, deterministic validation, review/correction, runtime validation, watchdog, checkpoint, and rollback with durable state and recovery.
findings.verificationMethod: Execute the full loop end to end and prove every mandated negative case blocks: missing specialist, stale review, unavailable builder, failed check, skipped state, unauthorized spend, stale lease, and rollback from a known-good checkpoint.
